## Claims
- [proved] **Theorem.** Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) be bigrassmannian, with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put
  \[
  q=n-r,\quad i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
  a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j),
  \]
  \[
  A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad Q=J_v/A_+J_v.
  \]
  Then both
  \[
  G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
  \]
  map to homogeneous integral bases of \(Q\). Hence both families minimally generate \(J_v\). In particular,
  \[
  Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z\,e_\rho,\qquad
  \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|,
  \]
  \[
  H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z,
  \]
  and \(Q_d\) is torsion-free. The basis \(e_\rho\) admits the perfect integral degree-complement pairing
  \[
  \langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee},\qquad
  \rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1),
  \]
  between \(Q_d\) and \(Q_{2ij+ab-d}\). The lower-family generation and its no-syzygy mechanism are grounded in the supplied full text. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235, 819-831]
- [unsupported] A parameter-uniform closed formula for the unimodular change-of-basis matrix from the ordered \(G_L\)-basis to the ordered \(G_R\)-basis is not established.

## Strategy

**Hypotheses.** The theorem uses precisely the bigrassmannian conditions and definitions in the claim. Here \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\); the case \(a=0\) means \(b^a\) contains only the empty partition.

**Dependency boundary.** The required lower-family integral indecomposables certificate is canonical accepted attempt `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1`. Quotient conjugation is `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1`; its application to the right-adjoined family, including conjugate-parameter admissibility, is `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1`. The Hilbert-series and pairing consequences agree with `research-attempt-research-plan-task-317-1`. No finite computation, including transition computations in degrees \(6,\ldots,10\), is used.

**Consolidated proof.** Let \(F_L\) be the graded free abelian group on \(G_L\), mapped to \(Q\). Generation gives a graded surjection \(F_L\twoheadrightarrow Q\). If its kernel contained a nonzero homogeneous element of added weight \(N\), then, after expressing its image in \(A_+J_v\) using generation by \(G_L\) and collecting degrees, one obtains a nonzero homogeneous syzygy
\[
\sum_{|\rho|=N}c_\rho\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}
=\sum_{|\lambda|<N}f_\lambda\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)},
\qquad \deg f_\lambda=N-|\lambda|>0.
\]
The accepted graded-kernel certificate verifies the necessary box nonvanishing, validity inequalities, large-\(N\) descent, and the \(a=0\) boundary; the no-syzygy theorem therefore forces all \(c_\rho=0\). Thus \(F_L\cong Q\).

Partition conjugation induces the accepted graded integral isomorphism
\[
Q_v\cong Q_{v^\vee}.
\]
It interchanges \(i,j\), preserves \(a,b\), and sends \(G_R(v)\) bijectively to \(G_L(v^\vee)\). Since the latter is an integral basis by the preceding paragraph, \(G_R(v)\) is an integral basis of \(Q_v\). A proper subfamily of either basis cannot generate \(Q\), hence cannot generate \(J_v\), proving minimality.

Finally, indexing the lower basis by \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) gives the Hilbert series. Complementation in \(b^a\) reverses weight from \(|\rho|\) to \(ab-|\rho|\); its permutation matrix gives the displayed perfect integral pairing.

**Verdict.** The requested target—minimality of both generating families, strengthened to integral homogeneous bases of \(J_v/A_+J_v\)—is established within the stated boundary.
